title: Marguerite and the Harvest
premise: Rafael Villalobos, a pest controller hired to deal with an infestation at the Villalobos family farmhouse, finds no vermin—only fingerprints appearing on the inside of sealed windows, and mirrors that lag a second behind reality. As the frost season deepens, Rafael realizes the 'pest' is the house itself, counting down its inhabitants through an inheritance ritual that claims one family member per generation. To survive, Rafael must convince the skeptical family to abandon their ancestral home before the first hard frost completes the count, even as the house begins erasing their memories of ever having lived there. In the end, Rafael burns the family ledger in the root cellar, breaking the inheritance, but the final mirror still shows one empty chair too many.
about_author: Coral Zhou is the pen name of a former agricultural inspector who spent a decade documenting abandoned farmsteads across the Midwest. Their fiction blends rural decay with domestic dread, and they insist every haunted house they write about was based on a real floor plan.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. A routine pest-control call to the Villalobos farmhouse turns strange when Rafael finds greasy fingerprints on the inside of boarded windows, three stories up. The family matriarch, Abuela Rosa, insists it's raccoons. Emotional beat: professional skepticism masking a first flicker of unease.

chapters.title: Doors Counted
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael's habit of counting doors on entry reveals twelve doors—but only eleven rooms. The youngest daughter, Marisol, mentions she counts them too, and sometimes gets thirteen. Emotional beat: the eerie comfort of finding someone else who notices.

chapters.title: What the Traps Catch
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Overnight traps come up empty except for one holding a curl of human hair braided around a splinter of window glass. Rosa burns it without explanation. Emotional beat: the family knows more than they're saying, and Rafael resents being managed.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. Marisol notices her reflection blinks after she does—a full second behind. She tests it with her brother Tomás; his mirror lags too. They agree not to tell their mother. Emotional beat: childhood complicity turning into shared dread.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Cellar
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Following scratching sounds, Rafael finds a root cellar containing a family ledger: names, dates, and frost patterns drawn beside each entry. Every generation ends with a name struck through. Emotional beat: horror shifting from phenomenon to inheritance.

chapters.title: Rosa's Version
chapters.summary: POV Rosa. Rosa recalls her own mother teaching her the count: keep the lights on, keep the doors counted, stay invisible to the house. She believes compliance has kept the family safe for ninety years. Emotional beat: loyalty to tradition as both shield and cage.

chapters.title: Frost on the Inside
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. First frost arrives—and forms on the interior windows, tracing patterns that match the ledger drawings exactly. The fingerprints reappear, now pressed into the frost from within the glass. Emotional beat: the countdown made visible.

chapters.title: Tomás Stops Sleeping
chapters.summary: POV Tomás. Tomás hears his name called from inside the walls each night, in his dead grandfather's voice. He starts sleeping in the truck. His mother calls it a phase. Emotional beat: a child's terror dismissed by adult denial.

chapters.title: Thirteen Doors
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. Marisol counts thirteen doors at dawn—the extra one standing open where a wall should be, breathing cold air. By afternoon it's gone, but the wallpaper remembers its outline. Emotional beat: proof that can't be kept.

chapters.title: The Van Won't Start
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael decides to leave and fetch help, but the van dies at the property line, engine flooded with something that smells like pond water and violets. Walking out, Rafael loses twenty minutes and arrives back at the porch without remembering turning around. Emotional beat: the realization that leaving was never permitted.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Rosa. Rosa finally explains: the house keeps the family alive in exchange for one name per generation, chosen by frost. Her sister was taken in 1974. She stayed because leaving means the house follows. Emotional beat: confession as betrayal—she knew all along.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: POV Tomás. Tomás wakes unable to remember his teacher's face, then his best friend's name. Photographs in the hallway are fading selectively, faces smearing like wet ink. Emotional beat: grief for memories he can feel slipping but cannot name.

chapters.title: The Second Mirror
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael covers every mirror, but that night finds one uncovered in a room Rafael is certain didn't exist yesterday. Its reflection shows the room occupied by figures standing perfectly still, waiting. Emotional beat: the watchers revealed; invisibility has failed.

chapters.title: Marisol's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. Marisol speaks aloud to the house, offering herself if it spares Tomás. The frost patterns rearrange into what looks like acceptance. Emotional beat: terrible courage—the child negotiating with the predator.

chapters.title: Rafael Breaks Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael stops keeping the count, leaves doors open, kills the lights—testing whether obedience matters. The house responds violently: every fingerprint in the house appears at once, thousands of them, all pointing toward the cellar. Emotional beat: defiance revealing the house's true center.

chapters.title: What Rosa Struck Through
chapters.summary: POV Rosa. Rosa reads the ledger closely and finds her own mother's handwriting beneath the entries: instructions for unmaking the count, torn out decades ago. The missing page is hidden in the lining of her wedding quilt. Emotional beat: hope arriving through the most painful inheritance.

chapters.title: The Quilt Page
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The recovered page reveals the ritual's flaw: the house requires a willing keeper. Burn the ledger before the final frost pattern completes, and the inheritance breaks—but the keeper who burns it takes the debt. Emotional beat: the cost made explicit, and Rafael choosing anyway.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rafael/Marisol. Final frost begins forming across every surface, spelling the last pattern. The family fights toward the cellar through rooms that rearrange, doors that lead back on themselves, mirrors showing them already frozen. Emotional beat: desperate momentum against a closing clock.

chapters.title: Burning the Count
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. In the cellar, surrounded by frost writing itself up Rafael's arms, Rafael feeds the ledger page by page into a propane flame. The house screams through every mirror at once. The frost stops one line short of completion. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice accepted, the count broken mid-stroke.

chapters.title: Evacuation
chapters.summary: POV Rosa. At dawn the family walks out; the van starts on the first try. Rosa looks back once and sees the house standing ordinary, windows dark, as if exhaling after a century of holding its breath. Emotional beat: release shadowed by everything the house took to be persuaded.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Tomás. Weeks later, memories return slowly—Tomás remembers his friend's name in a diner booth and cries into his pancakes. But Rafael has stopped appearing in photographs entirely, and doesn't mention it. Emotional beat: recovery incomplete; debts paid unevenly.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Living alone in a rented apartment, Rafael keeps the lights on and counts the doors out of habit. One night the bathroom mirror reflects the room one second late—and shows a place set at a table for someone who isn't there yet. Emotional beat: quiet, unresolved dread; the inheritance may have followed its new keeper home.
